text:
For a grounded conducting sphere the method of images replaces the induced charge distribution by an image charge  

\[
q'=-\frac{R}{d}\,q
\]

located at a distance  

\[
a=\frac{R^{2}}{d}
\]

from the centre, i.e. inside the sphere.  
The separation between the real charge \(q\) (at distance \(d\)) and the image charge is  

\[
s = d-a = d-\frac{R^{2}}{d}= \frac{d^{2}-R^{2}}{d}.
\]

The potential at the position of the real charge due to the image charge is  

\[
V_{\text{ind}} = \frac{k q'}{s}= \frac{k\left(-\frac{R}{d}q\right)}{\frac{d^{2}-R^{2}}{d}}
               = -\,\frac{k R q}{d^{2}-R^{2}} .
\]

The electrostatic energy of the system (real charge plus induced charges) is half the product of the charge and the potential it experiences from the induced charges:

\[
U = \frac12 q V_{\text{ind}} = \frac12 q\left(-\frac{k R q}{d^{2}-R^{2}}\right)
    = -\frac12\,\frac{k q^{2} R}{d^{2}-R^{2}} .
\]

Thus the net potential energy is  

\[
\boxed{U = -\frac12\,k q^{2}\,\frac{R}{d^{2}-R^{2}} }.
\]

This corresponds to option **(D)**.  

Answer: D.
